prompt.context_jp: 甘春総合病院の朝は、いつものように救急搬送のサイレンとともに動き出した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 甘春総合病院の朝___、いつものように救急搬送のサイレンとともに動き出した。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks the topic of this scene-setting sentence.

feedback.correct_en: は sets '甘春病院の朝' as the topic/frame the narrator will comment on — a classic scene-setting opener.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark the morning as new, exhaustive information, which doesn't fit this descriptive narration.

prompt.context_jp: ストレッチャーが救急口から検査室へと走り込んできた瞬間、五十嵐の視界の中心に、青ざめた杏の横顔が飛び込んできた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 五十嵐の視界の中心に、青ざめた杏の横顔___飛び込んできた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this sudden appearance.

feedback.correct_en: が introduces An's pale profile as new, striking information that suddenly enters Igarashi's field of vision.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat her profile as an already-established topic, losing the shock of the sudden sight.

prompt.context_jp: 周囲の看護師たちは慌ただしく処置に走り、部屋の空気は一気に張り詰めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 部屋の空気___一気に張り詰めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the room's atmosphere.

feedback.correct_en: は contrasts/frames '部屋の空気' as the topic whose state changes, paralleling the preceding clause about the nurses.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight the atmosphere as newly identified, but here the writer is commenting on a known element of the scene.

prompt.context_jp: 辻村駿太郎の声が飛び、看護師と技師が一斉に動きだす。
prompt.prompt_jp: 辻村駿太郎の声___飛び、看護師と技師が一斉に動きだす。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this introduction of Tsujimura's voice.

feedback.correct_en: が marks Tsujimura's voice as new information bursting into the scene and triggering action.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame his voice as an already-established topic, undercutting the sudden-event feel.

prompt.context_jp: 「政治家ですよ それも 超大物の 連日 ニュースになってるでしょ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 安野将司___政治家ですよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for identifying who Anno Shoji is.

feedback.correct_en: は takes '安野将司' as a known topic and provides new information about him (he's a politician).
feedback.incorrect_en: が would answer 'who is a politician?' — the wrong direction here, since the name is the known topic.

prompt.context_jp: 「ホントに あいつは 優秀な奴です 技師としてだけではなく 医者としても」
prompt.prompt_jp: あいつ___優秀な奴です。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle Onodera uses to describe Igarashi.

feedback.correct_en: は takes 'あいつ' (Igarashi) as the known topic and describes him — natural for sharing an opinion about a known person.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively identify him (THAT guy is the capable one), which doesn't fit the praise-as-comment context.

prompt.context_jp: 「彼女は 僕の患者です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女___僕の患者です。
prompt.prompt_en: Igarashi insists on his claim to An as patient. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は topicalizes '彼女' with an implicit contrast — 'as for her, (regardless of what you say) she is MY patient.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight her as newly identified, but Igarashi is pushing back on an existing claim about her.

contrast_examples.en: She is my patient. (asserting against pushback)

prompt.context_jp: 廊下の向こうから、革靴の乾いた足音が近づいてくる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 廊下の向こうから、革靴の乾いた足音___近づいてくる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the approaching footsteps.

feedback.correct_en: が introduces the footsteps as new sensory information entering the scene — a classic descriptive が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose the footsteps as a known topic, which clashes with their fresh appearance in the narration.

prompt.context_jp: 「安野先生との繋がりは お前の将来に必ず役に立つ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 安野先生との繋がり___お前の将来に必ず役に立つ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle Tsujimura's father uses here.

feedback.correct_en: は topicalizes 'the connection with Anno' and comments on its value — the father is explaining why it matters.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight it as newly singled out, but the father is making a general evaluative comment about a known item.

prompt.context_jp: 「患者に対する責任を負ってるのは 我々医師です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 患者に対する責任を負ってる___我々医師です。
prompt.prompt_en: Tsujimura asserts who bears responsibility. Choose the correct particle (after のは or が).

feedback.correct_en: のは cleft-topicalizes the action ('the ones who bear responsibility') and identifies the answer: us doctors. This is the natural 'it is X who...' structure.
feedback.incorrect_en: のが would be ungrammatical as the main-clause topic here — the cleft structure requires は.

contrast_examples.jp: 責任を負うのは医師だ。

prompt.context_jp: 「その頃から 甘春は お父さんみたいな放射線科医になるっていう 明確な夢を持って勉強してた」
prompt.prompt_jp: その頃から 甘春___お父さんみたいな放射線科医になるっていう 明確な夢を持って勉強してた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for how Tsujimura refers to An here.

feedback.correct_en: は sets 甘春 as the topic Tsujimura wants to comment on — he's describing her character as he remembers it.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively identify her among others, but he's giving background about a shared known person.

contrast_examples.en: It was An who was studying.

prompt.context_jp: 「関節部分に熱があり 関節の不安定さが残存しています」
prompt.prompt_jp: 関節部分に熱___あり、関節の不安定さが残存しています。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the finding Igarashi reports.

feedback.correct_en: が marks '熱' as new information — the existence of heat in the joint is the finding being reported.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose heat as a known topic, but Igarashi is introducing this clinical observation.

prompt.context_jp: 「治療方針を決めるのは 医師である僕です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 治療方針を決める___医師である僕です。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the correct particle (cleft structure).

feedback.correct_en: のは makes 'the one who decides treatment' the topic and identifies 'me, the doctor' as the answer — a classic 'it's X who...' cleft.
feedback.incorrect_en: のが does not form this identifying cleft; は is required for the cleft topic in this structure.

prompt.context_jp: 「患者のことは 僕が誰よりも分かってる」
prompt.prompt_jp: 患者のことは 僕___誰よりも分かってる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking '僕' in this emphatic claim.

feedback.correct_en: が exhaustively identifies '僕' as THE one who understands the patient better than anyone — a classic が-focus ('I, more than anyone else').
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make '僕' just a topic and lose the comparative emphasis; also the sentence already has は on '患者のこと'.

prompt.context_jp: 「二流大学出身のお前が うちで生き残るには 相応の覚悟が必要なんだ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 二流大学出身のお前が うちで生き残る___相応の覚悟が必要なんだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 生き残る.

feedback.correct_en: には sets up the condition/purpose ('in order to survive') as the topic for the comment that follows.
feedback.incorrect_en: にが is ungrammatical here; this frame requires は after に to topicalize the condition.

contrast_examples.jp: 生きるには金が必要だ。

prompt.context_jp: 「そうしたいからに 決まってるじゃない」
prompt.prompt_jp: 大森___微笑みながら、少しだけ椅子を近づけた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for Omori as the sentence's topic.

feedback.correct_en: は continues Omori as the known topic in the narration — she's already in the scene and the narrator describes her action.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would reintroduce her as new/identifying, but she's already the active participant in the ongoing conversation.

prompt.context_jp: 「うちの技師たちは 彼らは 麗洋病院が見落とした 胃がんを見つけたんだ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 麗洋病院___見落とした 胃がんを見つけたんだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle inside this relative clause.

feedback.correct_en: が is the standard subject marker inside a relative clause ('the cancer that Reiyo overlooked'). は cannot normally appear in a relative clause modifying a noun.
feedback.incorrect_en: は here would break the relative-clause structure; は tends to scope over the main clause, not an embedded modifier.

prompt.context_jp: 彼は胸に湧き上がる動揺を抑えきれず、思わず幼いころと同じ呼び方で名を呼んでしまう。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼は胸に湧き上がる動揺を___きれず、思わず名を呼んでしまう。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that collocates with 動揺 here.

feedback.correct_en: 抑えきれず ('unable to suppress') is the standard collocation for emotional turmoil (動揺).
feedback.incorrect_en: 止める and 隠す don't form the idiomatic 〜きれない pattern with 動揺 as naturally; 抑える is the fixed partner.

prompt.context_jp: 極秘入院という体裁で世論の目を欺こうと企てるその話に、鏑木の眉はわずかに動く。
prompt.prompt_jp: 極秘入院という___で世論の目を欺こうと企てる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word meaning 'outward appearance / pretext'.

feedback.correct_en: 体裁 (ていさい) means 'outward form / pretext', fitting the sense of disguising the hospitalization.
feedback.incorrect_en: 姿勢 means posture/attitude, and 気配 means sign/presence — neither captures the 'guise/façade' meaning.

prompt.context_jp: 「抜かりはございません 辻村教授」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___はございません、辻村教授。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word meaning 'oversight/slip'.

feedback.correct_en: 抜かりはございません is a set phrase meaning 'there is no oversight / we've got everything covered' — exactly what Kaburaki is assuring.
feedback.incorrect_en: 遅れ (delay) and 違い (difference/mistake) don't form this fixed reassurance idiom.

prompt.context_jp: 「がっかりさせないでくれよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___させないでくれよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that the father uses to warn his son.

feedback.correct_en: がっかりさせる means 'to disappoint'. The father is warning Shuntaro not to disappoint him.
feedback.incorrect_en: うっかり (careless) and しっかり (firmly) are adverbs and don't form 〜させる in this disappointment sense.

prompt.context_jp: 結局、方針は形だけの検査でお茶を濁すという線で落ち着いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 形だけの検査でお茶を___という線で落ち着いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb for the idiom meaning 'fudge/gloss over'.

feedback.correct_en: お茶を濁す is a fixed idiom meaning 'to give a vague answer / gloss over' — exactly the policy here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 流す and 入れる don't form this idiom; only 濁す works with お茶 for this meaning.

prompt.context_jp: 「このタイミングで発見できたのは 不幸中の幸いかと」
prompt.prompt_jp: このタイミングで発見できたのは ___の幸いかと。
prompt.prompt_en: Complete this four-character idiom.

feedback.correct_en: 不幸中の幸い is a set phrase meaning 'a silver lining / a bit of luck in misfortune'.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other options are not fixed expressions; only 不幸中の幸い is idiomatic.

prompt.context_jp: 「余計な詮索はしないこと 君たちには関係ありません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 余計な___はしないこと。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word meaning 'prying/snooping'.

feedback.correct_en: 詮索 (せんさく) specifically means 'prying into others' affairs', which fits 鏑木's warning.
feedback.incorrect_en: 検索 is 'search (database)' and 捜索 is 'search operation' — neither has the nosy connotation needed here.

prompt.context_jp: 「バリウムの二重造影は 技師の腕の見せどころだぞ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 技師の腕の___だぞ。
prompt.prompt_en: Complete this expression for 'a chance to show one's skill'.

feedback.correct_en: 腕の見せどころ is a fixed expression meaning 'a chance to show one's skill'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見どころ means 'highlight (of a show)'; 見せ場所 isn't a standard form. Only 見せどころ pairs with 腕.

contrast_examples.en: It's time to show my skill.

prompt.context_jp: 「大事なのは 立場とか場所とかじゃなく 何をするか なんじゃないかなって」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___なのは 立場とか場所とかじゃなく 何をするか なんじゃないかな。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the adjective meaning 'important'.

feedback.correct_en: 大事 means 'important' — fitting An's realization about what truly matters.
feedback.incorrect_en: 大変 means 'tough/awful' and 大体 means 'roughly' — neither fits the 'what's important is...' frame.

prompt.context_jp: Igarashi pushes back after being told technicians shouldn't give opinions; he insists on his responsibility for An.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for Igarashi's quiet but firm declaration?

choices.text: 彼女は 僕の患者です。
彼女が 僕の患者です。
彼女を 僕の患者です。

feedback.correct_en: は topicalizes '彼女' with implicit contrast — 'as for her, she is MY patient' — the natural pushback tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would answer 'which one is your patient?' which isn't the question. を is ungrammatical before a copula clause.

contrast_examples.jp: この人は僕の担当です。
contrast_examples.en: This person is under my charge.
This is the person in charge. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: Igarashi delivers a clinical finding to Dr. Tsujimura about An's shoulder.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for reporting the clinical finding?

choices.text: 関節部分に熱があり、関節の不安定さが残存しています。
関節部分は熱があって、関節の不安定さは残っています。
関節部分が熱で、関節の不安定さを残存します。

feedback.correct_en: The が + 残存しています phrasing is the standard clinical register for reporting findings — concise and formal.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses は twice and sounds overly casual/awkward for a report. C has wrong particles (が熱で is unnatural) and misuses 残存.

prompt.context_jp: Igarashi counters Tsujimura's claim that only doctors have responsibility.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for Igarashi's rebuttal?

choices.text: 医師に責任があるように 技師にも ちゃんとした写真を撮るという責任があります。
医師が責任あるから 技師もちゃんとした写真撮る責任あります。
医師は責任があって 技師はちゃんとした写真を撮ると責任があります。

feedback.correct_en: The 〜ように parallel structure elegantly contrasts the two roles while にも (also) extends responsibility to technicians.
feedback.incorrect_en: B omits particles (〜あるから without が properly placed, 撮る責任) and sounds choppy. C misuses と and loses the parallel.

contrast_examples.jp: 君と同じように私にも権利がある。
contrast_examples.en: Just like you, I also have rights.

prompt.context_jp: Tsujimura's father warns him before leaving.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural as a father's curt warning?

choices.text: がっかりさせないでくれよ。
がっかりしないでくれよ。
がっかりさせられないでくれよ。

feedback.correct_en: がっかりさせる = 'cause (me) to be disappointed'. The causative + 〜ないでくれ perfectly fits the father's 'don't let me down' tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: B means 'don't you get disappointed' — reverses who feels it. C mixes causative-passive and is ungrammatical here.

prompt.context_jp: Tsujimura thanks Igarashi after the successful surgery.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for 'thanks to your images'?

choices.text: あなたの写真のおかげです。ありがとう。
あなたの写真のせいです。ありがとう。
あなたの写真によってです。ありがとう。

feedback.correct_en: 〜のおかげです expresses gratitude for a positive result — the natural pairing with ありがとう.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜のせいです attributes blame (negative). 〜によってです is grammatically odd as a stand-alone statement of thanks.

contrast_examples.jp: 君のおかげで成功した。
